name: Zygoma-mandible angle

lead: The zygoma-mandible angle is a ratio-style measure drawn from the widest point of the cheekbone (zygoma) down to the jaw corner (gonion). Looksmaxxing posters use it to describe how the cheek and jaw widths relate in the face, and to think about why some cheekbone implants look natural and others look overdone.
The idea comes from a looksmax.org thread rather than from published literature. Related published work examines facial bone measurements in aesthetic surgery planning.

paras: People assess it from frontal photos by comparing the outer cheekbone point with the jaw angle, often alongside bizygomatic and bigonial width and facial height. It is mostly used as a thinking tool when discussing implant or jaw surgery plans.
As an analysis concept it carries no physical risk. Surgeries discussed alongside it, such as cheek implants and lower-face procedures, have their own surgical risks.

angle.text: People use the angle to compare how wide the cheekbones sit relative to the jaw and to decide how much projection or width suits their face when considering implants.

lead: The zygoma-mandible angle (ZMA) is a facial-analysis measure used in looksmaxxing communities. It describes the angle formed between the outermost point of the cheekbone and the jaw angle (gonion), and users treat it as a way to judge the harmony between mid-face width and jaw width. [1]

It was described in a looksmax.org thread in which the poster noticed, in AI-generated or edited surgical "morph" images, that faces looked better when the outer cheekbone and gonion were farther apart, and that cheekbone implants alone could look striking or uncanny. The poster hypothesized that the relationship between these points explains why implants are treated cautiously. [1] A reply questioned whether it was simply bizygomatic width; the poster answered that it accounts for facial height as well. [1]

In the clinical literature, aesthetic facial-bone surgery is increasingly planned with measurements of facial depth and bone contour, and patient-specific implants are designed with virtual planning. [2][3]
infobox: Cheek and jaw implant planning discussions

paras: The measure uses the lateral extreme of the zygomatic arch and the gonion on frontal photos. Its proposer argues that it adds information that bizygomatic width alone lacks because it relates to facial height. [1]

Discussion centers on why cheekbone implants can look "uncanny" and whether jaw widening or a lower-face downgraft balances them. One reply noted that people planning surgery typically already consider related ratios. [1]

No studies found on the zygoma-mandible angle by this name. A 2024 survey of 101 US participants rating 120 portraits sought new facial aesthetic measurements, including depth-based ones, for planning bone surgery and implants. [2] A 2025 review describes patient-specific facial cosmetic implants made via virtual surgical planning in silicone, titanium or porous polyethylene. [3]

lore.intro: The concept appears in a niche looksmax.org thread where it is offered as an underused ratio. [1]

claims.claim: The angle from outer cheekbone to gonion matters for looking good after zygomatic implants.
